title: Generation pattern for the text-to-video service
prompt: Users submit a prompt and get back a short generated video. Each render takes minutes of GPU time. Which generation pattern should the service use?
constraint: Video generation is extremely compute-heavy (minutes of GPU per render); cost control is paramount.

options.why: Decouples the request from the multi-minute GPU job, so workers can be batched, autoscaled to zero, and run on cheap spot/preemptible capacity — the best fit when cost control is paramount. No connection is held open burning idle resources, and queue depth becomes a direct knob on spend.

Improves perceived latency and lets users abort bad prompts before the expensive full render — which can save some GPU. But it adds a second pipeline and still needs an async path for the full render, so it raises complexity and cost without being the primary lever the constraint demands.
Pins an expensive GPU to a single open connection for minutes, blocking batching and autoscale-to-zero and risking timeouts — the worst possible choice when cost control is paramount.
Optimizes for latency at the direct expense of cost: idle pre-warmed GPUs bleed money continuously, which is exactly backwards given the constraint that cost control is paramount.
